Class DetourPlanner

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.DetourPlanner
All Implemented Interfaces:
NavigationListener
public final class DetourPlanner extends Object implements NavigationListener
Plans a mission's path for a Navigator and drives it around obstacles found on the way: the planner leJOS's PathFinder feeds a navigator through its WaypointListener, re-planning when the navigator says a leg ended at an obstacle, which leJOS leaves to the program.

The planner owns the mission, the waypoints to visit in order, and sends the navigator what is left of it. It listens to the navigator, so it is the navigator's NavigationListener; give it the program's own listener with setNavigationListener(NavigationListener), and it passes every call on. When a leg ends with MoveOutcome.OBSTACLE, it sidesteps from where the robot stopped. With the heading's forward direction u = (cos θ, sin θ), its left n = (−sin θ, cos θ), the robot at P and the obstacle r ahead:

  • the side is the one the next mission waypoint T lies on, the sign of the cross product u × (T − P), left on a tie;
  • the first detour point is the side step D1 = P + side · s · n, with s the robot's half width, the margin and half the obstacle's assumed width;
  • the second passes the obstacle, D2 = D1 + (r + depth + margin) · u;
  • then the rest of the mission, which the navigator reaches from wherever D2 left the robot, since it plans each leg from the measured pose.

A range finder measures distance, not width, so the obstacle's size is a guess: when the robot is blocked again on the way to the same mission waypoint, the next detour takes the other side, and the side step widens by one step every two detours: once, once, twice, twice. After the most detours for one waypoint, the planner gives up and passes the interruption on. The robot turns in place toward the side step, so the pilot's detector must stop it far enough from the obstacle to turn.

The navigator's path must hold the mission and the two detour points: an array two longer than the mission. The detour points are allocated here once; planning allocates nothing. The planner's calls come from the navigator's thread.
